messages.subject: Retrival of embedded phrases
parts:
Dear all,

I have got a problem that some of us may have encountered before. I need to retrieve phrases marked by brackets within rather long strings. For instance, in the sample input, I need to extract the PP but I only want the PP and not anything outside of it.

sampleinput <- c("(S (S (NP (N John)) (VP (V loves) (NP (N Mary) (PP (P from) (NP (N Switzerland)))))) (C and) (S (NP (N he)) (VP (V hates) (NP (N Jane)))))")

My desired output would be "(PP (P from) (NP (N Switzerland)))".

I obviously cannot use something like "(.*)". I cannot figure out the regex I need but I thought that some of you have already solved this issue. Could someone help me out?


Best
Martin

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Retrival of embedded phrases
parts:
Here you go:

library(stringr)

s <- c("(S (S (NP (N John)) (VP (V loves) (NP (N Mary) (PP (P from) (NP (N Switzerland)))))) (C and) (S (NP (N he)) (VP (V hates) (NP (N Jane)))))")

s.l <- str_replace_all(s, "\\(", "( ") %>% str_replace_all("\\)", " )") %>% strsplit(" ") %>% unlist()

extract.phrase <- function(s, ph){
    cpt <- c()
    capture <- 0
    for (l in s){
        if (l == ph){capture <- 1}
        if (capture > 0){
            cpt <- c(cpt, l)
            if (l == ")") {capture <- capture-1}
            if (l == "(") {capture <- capture+1}
        }
    }
    paste(cpt, collapse=" ")
}

extract.phrase(s.l, "PP")

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Retrival of embedded phrases
parts:
So, I guess a note of explanation:

First, we need to separate the sentence with spaces between the brackets (that's what the third line is doing. Then, a simple function goes through each item of the sentence, and if one of the items is the phrase you want to extract, then it starts capturing it into a vector by setting a counter capture. If the counter is > 0 it stores the value of the item it is currently at. When it finds a ")" it reduces the counter by 1, but when it finds a "(" it increases the counter by 1, so to balance the parenthesis. You can see it'll capture one extra parenthesis you'll have to remove. It will also capture ALL "PP"s (or whatever else you tell it to) in a sentence, without bounderies. You could easily fix this by adding an extra step to add a boundery whenever the counter is decreased to 0. I hope this helps
